title: Truthfulness of Scripture
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The truthfulness of Scripture means that God’s Word is true because God Himself is true. Scripture does not deceive, mislead, or fail, and it can be trusted in all that God intends it to teach.
summary: The truthfulness of Scripture means that God’s Word is true because God Himself is true. Scripture does not deceive, mislead, or fail, and it can be trusted in all that God intends it to teach.
christFocus: Jesus Christ prayed that God’s people would be sanctified by the truth and declared that God’s Word is truth. He is Himself the truth, and the Scriptures truthfully reveal His person, work, promises, and saving Gospel.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture is truthful because it comes from the God who cannot lie. God’s words reflect His character. Since He is holy, faithful, and true, His Word is trustworthy and reliable.

The truthfulness of Scripture gives believers confidence that God has not spoken carelessly. His promises are not empty. His warnings are not exaggerated. His commands are not corrupt. His Gospel is not uncertain. What God has revealed is worthy of faith.

This doctrine does not mean every passage is easy to understand or that every difficulty disappears immediately. It means that the problem is never dishonesty in God’s Word. Believers approach difficult passages with humility because God is true even when human understanding is limited.

The church must hold fast to Scripture’s truthfulness in every generation. When God’s Word is treated as unreliable, the Gospel is weakened, obedience becomes negotiable, and faith loses its anchor.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people have been lied to by others, by sin, by shame, by false teaching, or by their own fears. They need more than another opinion. They need a truthful Word from a truthful God.

The truthfulness of Scripture gives stability to believers who feel overwhelmed by confusion. God’s Word can be trusted when feelings rise and fall, when suffering clouds judgment, and when the world calls truth outdated or offensive.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Trust God’s Word more than your shifting emotions or the changing claims of the world. When Scripture confronts you, receive it as truth. When Scripture promises mercy, believe it. When Scripture warns against sin, take it seriously. Let the truth of God’s Word sanctify your mind, correct your path, and deepen your confidence in Christ.
